script.title: Where to Stay in Melbourne: What the Free Tram Zone Changes
script.hook_text: Your hotel can change your tram bill

beats.narration: Where you sleep in Melbourne can change what trams cost you.
First visit, three or four nights, mostly on foot? Look at CBD, Fitzroy or St Kilda.
CBD: trams inside the Free Tram Zone cost nothing. Check the PTV zone map for exactly where it ends. My opinion: it has less street character.
Fitzroy sits outside the zone, so you'll need a myki for trams. Good if your evenings are bars and cafés.
St Kilda is my skip as a first base. The 96 tram runs there from the CBD, but beach days add tram time both ways.
Check current times and routes on the PTV journey planner before you book.
Tell me your city and your constraint in the comments, and I'll build the plan in a future video.

check_notes.issue: Route 96 runs between St Kilda Beach and East Brunswick and passes through the CBD. Describing it as running from the CBD to St Kilda is imprecise and could mislead viewers about where the route starts and ends.
check_notes.fix: Say that Route 96 runs from St Kilda Beach through the CBD, then confirm the route and stops on the PTV journey planner.

check_notes.issue: Fitzroy is generally outside the Free Tram Zone, but the zone boundary runs close to the CBD edge and some stops are near it. The claim is stated as absolute without any hedge about boundary details, and the zone may change.
check_notes.fix: Say Fitzroy is generally outside the Free Tram Zone, that some stops sit near the boundary, and that viewers should check the current PTV zone map before booking.
